newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open higher on US, auto strength.
newsitem.headline: German shares open higher on US, auto strength.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade firmer on Monday following the stronger dollar and Friday's 1.58 percent gain on Wall Street.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares traded 40.12 points up at 2,899.40 just after the bourse start, with March DAX futures up 32.0 points at 2,914.0.

Shares had earlier breached the 2,900 level in pre-bourse electronic trade but fell back again with dealers saying the public holiday in the southern state of Bavaria, home to a number of large banks, was holding back dealing volumes.

"People are also looking to restructure their portfolios a bit for the year ahead and I wouldn't be surprised if there was now some form of consolidation," one dealer said, referring to recent strong gains in line with the U.S. share market.
Most activity was seen in the automotive sector, where a number of stocks were boosted by positive news emerging on the sector from the Detroit Motor Show.

Daimler-Benz gained 2.40 marks to 107.95 after its Mercedes unit, which accounts for most of parent company profits, told journalists in Detroit it expected to have beaten its 1996 north American sales target of 85,000 vehicles and saw 1997 U.S. sales at over 100,000 units.

Sports car-maker Porsche rose 30 marks to 1,365 and Volkswagen was up 15 marks to 652.00 as dealers said they were confident of more data suggesting strong growth in the sector over the rest of the week.
VW was also boosted by a report it was planning this year to build a new "mini-car" to compete in the small-car market, dealer said.
Utility Veba was also 2.40 marks stronger at 91.25 on a report it was seeking to develop its telecom activities with a 500 million mark deal to buy German cable group Urbana Telekommunikation.
German employment, gross domestic product (GDP) and new orders data due later in the week will however be studied closely for clues to the strength of any economic recovery.
